articles.title: Star Wars: Starfighter is going to be star-studded
articles.summary: The Verge is about technology and how it makes us feel. Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts.
articles.body: Production on Star Wars: Starfighter officially began today, and Lucasfilm has finally confirmed the other actors who will be bringing the film to life alongside Ryan Gosling. Lucasfilm announced today that Star Wars: Starfighters has added Flynn Gray, Matt Smith, Mia Goth, Aaron Pierre, Simon Bird, Jamael Westman, Daniel Ings, and Amy Adams to its cast. The studio also shared a (very grainy) image of Gosling and Gray on the movie’s set. [Image: In a statement about the casting news, director Shawn Levy said that he was beyond excited to begin crafting an “original adventure” for the franchise — one set a few years after the events of The Rise of Skywalker. “Star Wars shaped my sense of what story can do, how characters and cinematic moments can live with us forever,” Levy said. “To join this storytelling galaxy with such brilliant collaborators onscreen and off, is the thrill of a lifetime.”

articles.title: Persona 6 exists, and that’s all we know
articles.summary: At the Xbox Games Showcase, Atlus announced the long-awaited next entry in the JRPG series with Persona 6.
articles.body: This year’s Summer Game Fest turned out to be a good one for fans of Japanese RPGs. First, the conclusion of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy was announced at SGF Live, and now we have the long-awaited return of the Persona series. Atlus confirmed Persona 6 exists with a brief teaser, but aside from implying a very dark tone, that’s about all the video revealed. There’s no release date or window, though the game will be coming to the PS5, Xbox, and PC whenever it does launch. Atlus describes the game as “a bold, new standalone story blending heartfelt daily life and new characters with pulse-pounding, supernatural adventure,” which could also describe most Persona titles. Persona 6 will be the first all-new entry in the franchise since 2017. However, Atlus hasn’t exactly been dormant during that time. An enhanced version, Persona 5 Royal, launched in 2022, and the developer also put out a remake of Persona 3. Meanwhile, longtime Persona director Katsura Hashino led development on a different roleplaying game, the fantasy epic Metaphor: ReFantazio in 2024. articles.title: Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer
articles.summary: Mike Flanagan’s adaptation of Carrie updates the Stephen King classic for the modern age.
articles.body: Mike Flanagan’s latest Stephen King adaptation, Carrie (this will be his fourth), is slated to make its debut on Amazon Prime on October 7th. The new trailer dropped at Comic-Con 2026 and doesn’t contain many surprises. If you’re familiar with Carrie at all, it hits all the expected notes, though it’s clearly been updated for the modern era. According to Deadline, Flanagan’s take on the classic King novel will tackle very modern teen challenges like active shooter drills and bullying on social media. The director apparently invited high schoolers into the writers’ room, using their real-life traumas to inform the script: > “They shared shocking one-off situations or constant treatment and microaggressions and things that are not necessarily present themselves as targeted harassment. [We will dive into] the cruelty in today’s world and how the internet has encouraged cruelty, rewards and celebrates and amplifies it. This is awful for adults to deal with, and for teenagers even more so.” [Media: Brian De Palma’s iconic 1976 adaptation of Carrie is iconic and features an unimpeachable performance from Sissy Spacek. But it’s undeniable that Summer H. Howell, who was 21 at the time of shooting, is much more believable as a high school student than Spacek, who was 26 at the time.

articles.title: Bruce Campbell says he has 5 years to live 'give or take' amid cancer battle
articles.summary: Cult movie icon Bruce Campbell declined to share what type of cancer he has, but said that he has a life expectancy of five years 'give or take.'
articles.body:
Bruce Campbell has an update on his cancer battle, revealing that a recent prognosis expects he has five more years left to live.

During a Sept. 3 episode of " The Adam Carolla Show ," the 68-year-old actor, best known for his roles in "The Evil Dead" franchise, declined to share what type of cancer he has, but said that he has a life expectancy of five more years "give or take."

"I've decided though, pretty specifically, to live with it, not die from it," he told host Adam Carolla. "The cancer rabbit hole is enormous. You can go into focus groups of 10,000 guys who have exactly what you have. I won't touch it with a 10 foot pole."

Instead of going down the "massive rabbit hole," the Michigan-born actor said he will focus on promoting his new film "Ernie & Emma," an independent dramedy he wrote, directed, produced and stars in.

"I'm moving on. I got a movie to promote. And when I promote this movie, I have nothing. I'm free and clear when I promote this movie mentally," Campbell said. "You have to make this decision of, 'well, okay, but do I have to stop everything that I'm doing because of this?' Well, no."

Campbell added that he feels "perfect" right now as he continues to refuse to let his battle stop him from living life.

"The cancer, it creep me out because of the ancillary stuff that it does. It's not just, you don't die for cancer. You die from what cancer does to you," he continued.

Bruce Campbell said his cancer is 'treatable, not curable'

In March, Campbell opened up about his health battle in a statement shared on social media earlier this month, in which he said his cancer is "treatable, not curable."

"I apologize if that's a shock - it was to me. I'm not gonna go into more detail," he wrote. "I'm posting this because professionally, a few things will have to change - appearances and cons and work in general need to take back seat to treatment."

The cult movie icon said that he hoped to get well by the summer so he could tour for his new film, " Ernie & Emma ."

"It doesn't change anything for me," he told the Salem Statesman Journal , part of the USA TODAY Network, in March. "It makes you prioritize 100 percent, and for me, the priority is this movie."

"Ernie & Emma" follows a small-town pear salesman who embarks on a "journey of challenging and reflective escapades" as he follows a detailed list of instructions for what to do with his late wife's ashes, according to the film synopsis .

articles.title: New photos mark Prince George's first day at the school his dad William attended
articles.summary: The future king is starting at Britain's prestigious, $85,000-a-year boarding school, where famous former students include Eddie Redmayne and Tom Hiddleston.
articles.body:
Prince George has followed in the footsteps of his father, Prince William, and started at the U.K.'s most elite school.

The 13-year-old royal, who is second in line to the British throne, began at Eton College on Tuesday, marking the next phase of his education. The future king arrived at school with his parents and was greeted by the headteacher Simon Henderson, who told George, "Welcome, good luck, enjoy it."

George wore a dark suit with a blue shirt and tie, but will change into "school dress," a black tailcoat, vest and pinstriped pants with a stiff white collar.

Three photographs of George, wearing his uniform, were released by Kensington Palace to mark the occasion. Taken by one of the family's go-to professional photographers, Matt Porteous, the images were shot before George's arrival at school on Tuesday for the start of the new term.

Eton isn't your average private school. The institution, which charges about $85,000 a year in fees, is a centuries-old boarding school that has, for generations, served as a leadership training ground for the British ruling classes.

Founded in 1440 by King Henry VI, it is one of the most famous educational institutions in history. Despite its name, it's not a university but rather a school for boys ages 13 to 18.

Eton is more than tuition fees, blazers and a competitive admissions process — it's a cultural institution. And it comes with a yearbook to die for. Whether that's Hollywood royalty such as Eddie Redmayne or Tom Hiddleston, former British prime ministers (20 have been educated at Eton) or any host of industry leaders across finance, media and fashion, the list goes on.

Along with Hiddleston and Redmayne, other A-list former students include Hugh Laurie, Damian Lewis and Dominic West. Nineteen Eighty-Four novelist George Orwell and James Bond author Ian Fleming also attended the school.

Most Eton alumni remain tight-lipped about their time at the school, but some former students have shared snippets of what life there was like. Redmayne's time at Eton crossed over with William's — in fact, the pair played on the same rugby team. The actor told Glamour in 2015 that William's "a wonderful man" and added that he "always felt slightly sorry for him because everyone wanted to tackle the future king of England."

While Lewis has spoken about the lifelong friendships "forged in the furnace" at Eton, West has shared how difficult it can be for some children to be sent away from home. Writing in the Radio Times in 2016, the actor said that going to boarding school had a "major effect" on him and was "the worst feeling I ever had," comparing it to grief after his parents died.

For William and Kate, the school's location was likely appealing. Situated in the town of Eton, just across the river from Windsor Castle, it's a 15-minute drive from George's family home, Forest Lodge, in Windsor Great Park, about 20 miles west of central London. Despite its proximity to his house, George will board at the school, the BBC reports .

The decision to send George to Eton was not a foregone conclusion, with the family reported to have looked at other schools in recent months , including the coeducational school Marlborough College, the alma mater of George's mother, Kate. Instead, they have chosen the same school his dad attended in 1995.

When King Charles and Princess Diana sent William to Eton in 1995, it broke with decades of royal tradition. Charles himself had attended Gordonstoun School in Scotland (close to the royals' Balmoral Castle), as had many of William's relatives, including his grandfather Prince Philip, his uncles Prince Andrew and Prince Edward, and his cousins Peter Phillips and Zara Tindall.

William has spoken fondly of his time at Eton, saying he particularly enjoyed visiting his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, at her Windsor Castle home. "She had the best teas ever, so I'd get well fed," he told Eugene Levy during an episode of Apple TV's The Reluctant Traveler in October 2025. During a BBC interview marking his 18th birthday, William said he had enjoyed the school "very much," particularly being able to move around the school "as just any other student" — a rare taste of normality for a future king.

The school day starts around 7 a.m. with breakfast in the boarding house, which is followed by an hour at Chapel. Lessons end at 5 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Tuesdays and Thursdays are half-days, but pupils also study for half a day on Saturdays.

The school has 25 boarding houses, each accommodating about 55 pupils and supervised by a staff member called a house master, a faculty member who oversees a boarding house. Each boy is given his own private room.

George is second in line to the throne, so the decision about which school he attends had to balance modern family life with aristocratic tradition. He was previously educated at Lambrook, a coeducational private school an eight-minute drive from his home, which he attended alongside his siblings, Charlotte and Louis.

When George's enrolment at Eton was announced in June, Melanie Sanderson, the managing editor of the Good Schools Guide, told the BBC that an Eton education "represents the best preparation for life as a modern working royal."

She added that "despite its ancient buildings, it's a modern school with a progressive outlook" and features "spectacular facilities and spacious grounds."

Perhaps unsurprisingly, an Eton College education doesn't come cheap. The school's current published 2025-26 fee is £21,099.60 ($28,301.99) per term. There are three terms in the British academic year, so the total cost is about £63,298.80 ($84,906.53) a year.

That figure excludes extras, such as activities, which can add another £1,500 ($2,012.14) per term.

articles.title: 'Practical Magic 2' review: Sequel honors the original by being a similarly dopey mess
articles.summary: The original "Practical Magic" wasn't a great film — but its fans might appreciate this similarly muddled sequel more than our film critic did.
articles.body:
Practical Magic was nobody's idea of a success when it hit theaters way back in 1998 — its box office take was modest at best, and critics were not kind to it. Its cozy fall vibes, (some rather mixed) messaging about sisterhood and female empowerment and fun performances from superstars Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, however, led it to become a seasonal staple on cable television, and it eventually found enough of an audience for a high-profile, nearly-30-years-later sequel to make financial sense in our nostalgia-obsessed world.

I watched the original for the first time ahead of the screening of the new one, and found it to be a tonally confused, badly paced mess, despite committed work from the lead actors, as well as from Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing as the aunts. The movie is decidedly uninterested in witchcraft, except as a means of advancing its story of love and loss — a potent idea, but one that gets buried beneath various subplots with wildly different tones. Centering this story on two women who are uniquely powerful but must hide it from society lest they be labeled witches is also an interesting concept, though it's muddled by the fact that these women are, canonically, witches.

In Practical Magic 2, based on the fourth book in the popular series by Alice Hoffman , the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all. In the original film, the Owens sisters discover a family curse that causes all the men they truly love to die, leading them to adopt two different lifestyles to cope with it. Now, this curse has passed down to Bullock's children, with disastrous consequences.

All the principal actors are back, except for Evan Rachel Wood as one of Bullock's daughters, who was replaced by Joey King , since the characters are meant to be in college. Bullock and Kidman have fantastic chemistry in the movie, and that energy has carried over to the press tour, with viral clips dominating the web in the run-up to the movie's release. Bullock has kept herself so scarce cinematically that seeing her onscreen is always exciting; she feels like one of the few true movie stars we have left who hasn't completely oversaturated the market or overstayed their welcome.

I acknowledge that these movies are not really for me — I want my movies about witches to do more with the dark arts than make margaritas and flicker the lights — and this sequel will likely satisfy fans who are simply eager to spend more time with these characters and their world. I found the movie's use of the legacy-sequel framework uninspiring and was never fully engaged with the story, which I felt hewed too closely to the original, both in content and in the way it's all so loosely connected.

The biggest issue, though, is with the screenplay. The movie is so all over the place that a "villain" is introduced and dealt with within a 10-minute span, then the movie climaxes, ostensibly wrapping everything up, only to go on for another 20 minutes that are absolutely useless and deadly. The plotting on the way there is as perfunctory as it gets, involving a magic book and a trip abroad to find answers dating back to their ancestral home.

Practical Magic 2 is just as dopey as the first movie — arguably more so — but it's certainly going to fare far better than its predecessor at the box office. But hey, I'm all for studios like Warner Bros. mining their back catalogs for unexpectedly viable IP and capitalizing on cult fandom. People who love the first film will likely have a good enough time, and the box office could also use a Sandra Bullock infusion. The best we can hope for is that the next legacy sequel, plucked from onetime obscurity and based on a cable-TV-era cult classic, finds a more compelling reason to exist.

Practical Magic 2 opens Friday, Sept. 11.

articles.title: Kelly Osbourne Recalls Being Given Her ‘First Line of Cocaine’ from One of Late Dad Ozzy’s Famous Rocker Friends
articles.summary: Kelly looks back at the family’s history with West Hollywood’s Sunset Marquis Hotel in the ‘If These Walls Could Rock’ documentary
articles.body:
Kelly Osbourne recalled the first time she was given a line of cocaine, which came from one of her late dad Ozzy's rocker friends

"I could never tell my parents because they would f---ing kill him," the actress and reality TV star said of the individual in the If These Walls Could Rock documentary

Kelly Osbourne shared a story about the first time she tried cocaine in the new documentary If These Walls Could Rock .

In the film, which looks back at the storied history of West Hollywood's Sunset Marquis hotel, the actress and reality star recalls spending the summer at the venue.

Kelly, 41, said that the Sunset Marquis was "the only hotel that my dad could stay in, at the time, where my dad could be himself."

"We'd be kicked out of everywhere, but not the Sunset Marquis," she said, adding: "My dad could misbehave politely here."

Kelly said that during that time she "felt like a little Eloise" as she explored the hotel. Later, it also became home to her teenage antics.

She recalled having her "first drink" and "first kiss" at the hotel, among other things.

"I did my first line of cocaine in this hotel… which was given to me by one of my dad's friends in a very very very big band, and I could never tell my parents because they would f---ing kill him," Kelly added.

Elsewhere in the documentary, Sharon Osbourne spoke about the family's stays at the hotel each summer while Ozzy Osbourne toured in the U.S., before they made permanent roots in Los Angeles.

The hotel maintained the rocker's "sex, drugs and rock 'n' roll" vibe, but also worked for the family at the time.

"He would love it here because he could wander. He could wander around outside in the garden. In those days he'd smoke," said Sharon, 73.

At the time, the TV personality and businesswoman said her late husband would greet the people staying in different bungalows as he wandered around.

"It was like you were in your own home with a lot of friends," said Sharon.

In a recent interview with Hello! magazine , Kelly opened up about trading the American West Coast for the English countryside.

"Being home in the U.K. has changed a lot for me," Kelly said of moving back to the U.K. "I've never been a California girl. It's been great to be home, and making a life for me and my son where I can see he's truly happy."

She also noted that the increase in gun violence in the United States impacted her decision to relocate.

"I don't ever want to have to explain to my son what to do during a gun raid," she said of her 3½-year-old son, Sidney , whom she shares with ex-fiancé Sid Wilson.

If These Walls Could Rock is currently available on Apple TV and Amazon Prime Video .

articles.title: Alex Van Halen calls Sammy Hagar 'a complete idiot' as decades-long feud between bandmates deepens
articles.summary: Alex Van Halen called Sammy Hagar "a complete idiot" in a new interview, and Hagar fired back with a pointed Instagram comment over the weekend.
articles.body: Alex Van Halen has some thoughts about former bandmate Sammy Hagar. During an interview with Brazilian music journalist Marcelo Vieira published earlier this month, Alex ripped into Hagar when asked about his 2011 memoir, "Red: My Uncensored Life in Rock." "I don't know what he wrote, and I don't wanna know," he said, according to a translation from the original Portuguese interview published by Roadie Crew. "In my opinion, Sammy Hagar is a complete idiot." SAMMY HAGAR BURIES DECADES-LONG FEUD WITH DAVID LEE ROTH AFTER TOUR DATES ARE AXED Hagar has since responded to the insult, writing in an Instagram comment over the weekend, "This comment and post is so unnecessary at this time in our lives, but I guess the truth hurts sometimes. Peace already." The latest jab comes after years of tension between the former bandmates, who have not spoken in more than two decades, according to Hagar. ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK MAKES BLUNT ADMISSION ABOUT MYSTERIOUS DECADES-LONG TOM JONES FEUD A representative for Alex did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Alex previously rejected an invitation to join Hagar and former Van Halen bassist Michael Anthony for their 2024 "Best of All Worlds" tour, which celebrated Hagar's era with the band. "I'm not interested," Alex told Billboard at the time. "They're not doing the band justice. They can do what they want to do. That's not my business." Alex also largely focused on Van Halen's original lineup with David Lee Roth in his 2024 memoir, "Brothers," while largely omitting Hagar's decade-long run with the band. GEORGE MICHAEL STRUGGLED WITH 'ETERNAL CONFLICT' OVER FAME, WHAM! BANDMATE ANDREW RIDGELEY SAYS "What happened after Dave left is not the same band," Alex told Billboard while promoting the book. "I'm not saying it was better or worse or any of that.… But the magic was in the first years, when we didn't know what we were doing, when we were willing to try anything." Earlier this year, Hagar suggested he would "never play" with Alex again more than 20 years after their last tour together. "I'm the biggest Pink Floyd fan. I see David Gilmour say, 'I will never play with Roger Waters again,' and I know what he means," the 78-year-old told Classic Rock. "I feel that way about Alex Van Halen. They're negative people." He later reunited with the group in 2004 for a reunion tour. The singer has suggested that Alex's health problems and inability or unwillingness to continue playing drums may have contributed to the tension. Hagar speculated that Alex could be frustrated that he and Anthony continue to perform Van Halen songs while the drummer is no longer touring. Hagar told Rolling Stone in April 2025 that he and Alex had not spoken in 21 years. "I hate to say it, but I dreamt about Alex the other night, man," he told the magazine. "It was crazy. articles.title: Autonomous racecars wreck at Imola.
articles.summary:

articles.title: Lori Loughlin files for divorce from husband Mossimo Giannulli
articles.summary: Lori Loughlin officially filed for divorce from Mossimo Giannulli after nearly 30 years of marriage.
articles.body:
Lori Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli are officially going their separate ways.

The " Full House " alum, 62, filed for divorce from her husband of nearly 30 years on Friday, Sept. 4, according to documents obtained by USA TODAY. Loughlin cited irreconcilable differences and listed their date of separation as Aug. 31, 2025.

She also revealed she and Giannulli have a prenuptial agreement regarding separate and community property, and indicated they will determine the issue of spousal support at a later date.

The former couple have been married since November 1997 and share daughters Olivia Jade Giannulli , 26, and Isabella Rose Giannulli , 27. In October, the actress' publicist confirmed to USA TODAY that she and the fashion designer were living separately , but no legal action had been taken at the time.

The divorce comes seven years after Loughlin and Giannulli were charged in the infamous Varsity Blues college admissions scandal in 2019. The parents later admitted to paying half a million dollars to get both their daughters into the University of Southern California as crew recruits despite neither child having played the sport.

Loughlin ultimately pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, while Giannulli pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud and honest services wire and mail fraud. She served two months in prison in late 2020, and he served a five-month sentence from November 2020 until being released on home confinement in April 2021.

After news of the pair's separation broke last year, Loughlin's former "Full House" costar John Stamos slammed Giannulli in an interview on Josh Peck's " Good Guys " podcast, alleging Giannulli was responsible for getting Loughlin involved in legal trouble.

"She's not a liar. She's a saint," Stamos said, adding, "She didn't deserve to be dragged through that. I know for a fact it was all him."

"There comes a point in a woman's life when choosing herself is no longer an option, it becomes necessary," she wrote in a lengthy statement on Instagram . "I share this not for sympathy, retaliation, or to publicly tear anyone down. I share it because too many women are taught to question themselves before they question what is happening right in front of them." The "Mr. Robot" actor has not commented on the allegation publicly. The couple welcomed a son in 2025.

When the scandal became public in 2019, Loughlin was fired by Hallmark and largely remained out of the spotlight. She made her return to acting in 2021 when she reprised her role from "When Calls the Heart " in its spinoff series, "When Hope Calls."

In December, Hallmark announced that Loughlin would return to "When Calls the Heart." She recently came back to social media as well with a joint Instagram post on Aug. 31, alongside five of her former "Full House" costars: Dave Coulier , Andrea Barber , Candace Cameron Bure , Jodie Sweetin and John Stamos .

articles.summary: Jelly Roll was formally uninvited from a Mar-a-Lago law enforcement fundraiser after his jokes about President Donald Trump while guest-hosting "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"
articles.body: Country artist Jelly Roll was formally uninvited to a fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago in November hosted by Law Enforcement Today to support the Federal Law Enforcement Offices Association (FLEOA) Foundation on Friday, following his stint on Jimmy Kimmel's show. Law Enforcement Today's Kyle Reyes told Fox News Digital that Jelly Roll didn't respond to the invitation sent on April 26, 2026, on behalf of FLEOA, but that they wanted to withdraw it in the wake of the Kimmel segment. The invitation, obtained by Fox News Digital, asked Jelly Roll if he would consider performing a few worship songs to close out the Big Blue Bash. A source told Fox News Digital that Jelly Roll's team was never reached or spoken to about the November event and said they found out about it on social media. The event is scheduled to take place in November at Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in Palm Beach, Florida. Law Enforcement Toady is running the gala to raise money for FLEOA and the FLEOA Foundation. The president of FLEOA said in a statement included on the Big Blue Bash invitation, "FLEOA is a non-partisan, professional association committed to supporting law enforcement across all agencies and administrations." JOHN RICH CLAIMS JELLY ROLL KNEW HE’D LOSE HALF HIS FANS OVER POLITICAL COMMENTS "It's a God-centered Gala and there's no better way to close out our event than with your voice," the letter to Jelly Roll read. Reyes withdrew the invitation after the country music artist's stint on Kimmel's late-night show in August. Reyes, who runs the Blue Lives Matter account on X, posted on Friday, "On April 26, 2026, we made the mistake of sending a formal invitation to country artist Jelly Roll to perform at this year's Second Annual Big Blue Bash at Mar-A-Lago, the home of President Trump." "The event is a fundraiser for the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Foundation, a 501(c)(3) that takes care of the families of wounded and fallen officers," he continued. "Our organization, which owns the largest police news outlet in the world, is running the event. We'll be joined by the heads of all of the federal law enforcement agencies, sheriffs, police chiefs and supporters." "This year's theme is American Superheroes, and we'll be joined by superheroes such as Lou Ferrigno (The Incredible Hulk), Dean Cain (Superman) and Kevin Sorbo (Hercules). We're formally withdrawing the invitation for Jelly Roll," Reyes added. The country star guest-hosted "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" and took aim at Trump's weight, physical fitness and approval ratings. "Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again," Jelly Roll said. "It’s crazy. Think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump." JELLY ROLL PICKED A FIGHT WITH TRUMP FANS AND MAY HAVE BUD LIGHTED HIMSELF "And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing," he added, before talking about the reaction to jokes he made about the president in a previous show, and said Trump should be able to "handle a few jokes." During his final show filling in for Kimmel, Jelly Roll walked back his previous assertions that he is apolitical and said, "A lot of people seem to think these Jimmy Kimmel writers have secretly been pulling the strings and forcing this good old country boy to poke fun at our commander in chief." And for some reason, that seemed to freak a lot of people out. I guess now that I’ve lost all this weight, folks can finally see I have balls," he said. 'NOT ON OUR WATCH': GLOBAL LAW ENFORCEMENT LEADERS UNITE IN POLAND AGAINST HATE "Sure, I lean left on some things," he continued. "But like most folks, I’m pretty down the middle. I am a Christian. I am a country music singer. I’m a farmer. I’m a bow hunter. And most of the things I eat, I prefer to get with a stick and a string. That’s the truth." He concluded the segment of his monologue by joking about his newfound friendships with Kimmel’s crew and said, "And I truly am going to miss all of my communist, Antifa friends here on the staff of ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’" Reyes addressed the Trump jokes in his social media post, writing, "What I saw last week with this self-absorbed 'artist' bashing President Trump and Conservatives was not a man who walks in the footsteps of Jesus Christ — it was a man desperately seeking attention and relevancy from the very Godless crowd that has categorically rejected his preaching." Prince Harry reportedly angered his father, King Charles, by informing British security officials of his UK return before telling his family.

Charles is frustrated by the lack of communication and fears that Harry and Meghan’s potential documentary deal with the BBC could further strain their relationship.

The King is concerned about the impact of Harry and Meghan’s return on the Royal Family’s public image and wants to maintain a positive relationship with his son and grandchildren.

Prince Harry 's surprise UK move has reportedly angered several family members. According to RadarOnline , Harry's father, King Charles , is "furious" after learning that the Duke of Sussex allegedly informed British security officials of his return first.

Harry apparently reached out to the Home Office in early August to get a head start on security for himself, Meghan Markle , and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, five. Charles learned of their move a few days later.

"The King understands perfectly well why the appropriate authorities needed advance warning, particularly given Harry's long-running concerns about security," a royal source told the outlet. "What angered him and made him furious was discovering that officials apparently knew something as significant as his son's return before he did."

The insider noted that, "after everything that has happened between them, Charles regarded that as extremely disappointing. This isn't some routine visit lasting a couple of days – Harry is bringing his wife and children back to Britain."

Another insider emphasized the "frustration" Charles feels, given that he and Harry "had finally begun making some progress personally." The source added, "The King wants a relationship with his son and particularly wants opportunities to see his grandchildren. Against that background, finding himself further down the information chain than the Home Office was never going to improve matters."

Charles' agitation comes shortly after senior royal sources revealed that the King would be even more furious if Harry and Meghan's UK return results in a documentary deal with the BBC. In a separate report from RadarOnline , the couple is now "exploring opportunities with British broadcasters" to expand their media portfolio, and a contract with the BBC is a possibility.

"The prospect of Harry and Meghan working with the BBC would inevitably cause anxiety at the Palace," one source explained. "Charles has been trying to rebuild his relationship with his son privately, and the last thing he wants is another television project generating headlines about the Royal Family. If it became another vehicle for discussing private royal matters, he would be furious."

A palace insider said, "The BBC carries a significance that another streaming service simply doesn't. It is Britain's national broadcaster and has a longstanding relationship with the monarchy. Seeing Harry and Meghan potentially earning substantial money from it would be difficult enough – seeing them discuss royal business would be another matter entirely."

Harry and Meghan's productions have mostly struggled to gain attention, but according to a senior UK television source, "Being back in Britain completely changes the landscape for Harry and Meghan. They don't need another gigantic Netflix-style agreement. They can potentially make individual programs with the BBC or commercial broadcasters and retain much greater freedom over what they produce."

articles.title: Penélope Cruz Sobs and Kisses Javier Bardem as ‘Bunker’ Dazzles Venice With Record 15.5-Minute Ovation
articles.summary: Penelope Cruz broke out into uncontrollable sobs as she kissed her husband and co-star Javier Bardem during the incredibly long 15.5-minute standing ovation...
articles.body:
Penelope Cruz broke out into uncontrollable sobs as she kissed her husband and co-star Javier Bardem during the incredibly long 15.5-minute standing ovation at the premiere of "Bunker" at the Venice Film Festival Tuesday night.

That made "Bunker" the winner of Venice 2026 (so far) for the most enthusiastic reception, and it fell just shy of one of the longest standing ovations of recent memory for Pedro Almodovar's "The Room Next Door' (which had the Lido crowd clapping for 17 minutes in 2024).

As the ovation raged on past the 10-minute mark, Cruz mouthed "Thank you!" to fans and paused to shake the hand of one particularly enthusiastic admirer behind her. As they finally made their exit, Cruz paused on the way out of the Palazzo del Cinema to say "Ciao!" to fans and graciously accept their praise. Director Florian Zeller instructed his cast, which included Patrick Schwarzenegger and Paul Dano, to individually step forward and receive applause during the ecstatic reception.

"Bunker" stars Bardem and Cruz as a married couple navigating professional and personal turmoil in the London home they share with their kids. Their marriage begins to unravel after Miguel, an architect, agrees to build a survivalist bunker for Andrew, a tech billionaire played by Dano. The morally dubious assignment opens up a rift between the couple after 17 years together, as Sofia begins questioning whether they still share the same values and starts working with a handsome American novelist Jeremy Gray (Schwarzenegger).

Cruz, wearing a ravishing red dress, collected flowers from fans and posed for selfies on the carpet beforehand. With its glamorous cast and Zeller's auteur pedigree, "Bunker" ranks among the biggest international movies hitting the fall festival circuit this year.

The film also brings Zeller back to Venice, where "The Son" competed for the Golden Lion in 2022. Zeller was already an acclaimed playwright when he made a successful leap into cinema with "The Father," which won a pair of Oscars for Anthony Hopkins' lead performance and for best adapted screenplay, shared by Zeller and Christopher Hampton. "Bunker" is arguably his most personal yet expansive film to date.

Sony Pictures Classics acquired rights to "Bunker" for North America, among other territories, and is planning an awards-qualifying run at the end of the year ahead of an early 2027 U.S. theatrical release. The company — which previously campaigned for "The Father" that earned six Oscar nominations, including best picture — is certainly hoping Cruz and Bardem's visceral performances in the film will propel it in the awards conversation.

The film is produced by Federica Sainte-Rose and Zeller through their Blue Morning Pictures, a Mediawan banner, alongside Fernando Bovaira and Simon de Santiago of MOD Producciones. FilmNation Entertainment is handling international sales.

Zeller told Variety in an interview before Venice that Stanley Kubrick's "Eyes Wide Shut" was a key inspiration for the film. Like Kubrick, who cast the then-married Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman as a couple whose relationship is unraveling, Zeller wanted to exploit the permeability between fiction and reality by putting Cruz and Bardem — partners for nearly two decades — on screen as husband and wife.

"I loved 'Eyes Wide Shut,' this ambivalent proposition presented to the audience where you're not quite sure what you're being invited to watch," Zeller said. With Cruz and Bardem, he wanted to use "what they are to touch on something more authentic and more unsettling for the audience."

The film also takes aim at the extreme wealth and isolation of the billionaire class, with Zeller saying Cruz brought her own "genuine anger" toward tech billionaires to Sofia. But rather than turning "Bunker" into an overtly political film, Zeller lets those larger themes gradually seep into the marriage at its center.

The story of "Bunker," which was inspired by the 2009 movie "The Man Next Door," soon grew beyond the central couple. While "Bunker" retains the psychological intensity that has become Zeller's signature, it is also more overtly political than his previous work, looking at how socio-economic anxieties are shaping contemporary relationships and family dynamics.

articles.title: Casey Affleck Reveals His and Ben Affleck’s Dad Timothy Died Earlier This Year
articles.summary: The news follows the Affleck family’s announcement on July 24 that Ben and Casey’s mother Chris died at 83 on June 2
articles.body:
Casey Affleck revealed publicly that his and Ben Affleck's father Timothy died in the last year during a Venice Film Festival press conference on Tuesday, Sept. 8

The Affleck family previously announced on July 24 that Ben and Casey's mother Chris died at 83 on June 2

Timothy and Chris divorced when Ben and Casey were children, and Casey said he "really wanted to show" his new movie Company to his parents

Casey Affleck revealed publicly that his and Ben Affleck 's father Timothy Affleck died in the last year during a Venice Film Festival press conference on Tuesday, Sept. 8.

Casey, 51, appeared in Venice alongside his girlfriend Caylee Cowan and sons Atticus and Indiana and others from the cast of his new movie Company , a Gothic and vampire-inspired movie that marks Casey's third film as a director. Ben also made an appearance to support his brother.

During a press conference, Casey stated that he dedicated the movie to both of his parents and indicated that both died this year. (Casey and Ben's mother Chris Affleck died at 83 on June 2, which the family announced on July 24.)

"It's dedicated to my parents because I lost both my mom and my dad this year, and they were very important to me," Casey said during the press conference, in response to a question from an Italian journalist. "I really wanted to show this movie to them, and I didn't get to. I think they would have liked it."

Casey and Ben's father Timothy and mother Chris divorced when Ben, now 54, was around 11 or 12 years old. According to a 2000 interview with Ben in The New York Times , Timothy once performed in the Theater Company of Boston alongside actors like Blythe Danner, Robert Duvall and Dustin Hoffman and was an aspiring playwright who often worked odd jobs and struggled with alcoholism.

At that time, the Times reported that Timothy had been sober since 1990 and was working as a counselor at a California-based alcohol rehabilitation center. "The most enduring lesson my father taught me is the degree to which it's possible to change your life and patterns," Ben said in that interview.

In February 2020, Ben told PEOPLE that Timothy had been sober for 30 years and described his sobriety as "the principal lesson and legacy of his life — is that he dramatically improved it."

" Part of being an adult is learning that your parents are just people . They're not perfect. They were just doing their best. As a child, we expect perfection out of our parents," he said at the time.

He continued, "I learned to be able to look at things that I wish were different about my childhood and say they [my parents] did their best. They were dealing with their own stuff and their own childhood trauma. The goal is to try and break some of these painful cycles."

A source told PEOPLE in July that Chris' death was " hitting Ben and Casey really hard ." According to an obituary the Affleck family shared at the time of Chris' death, she was given six months to live in December 2025 and wanted to live to see Casey's son Atticus graduate high school. (Casey shares his two sons with ex-wife Summer Phoenix .)

Per that obituary, Chris died two days after she attended the graduation ceremony with her family on May 31. She died from cardiopulmonary arrest while "visiting her son's residence," according to a death certificate obtained by PEOPLE.

In Venice, Casey said that he pours his own life experiences into his movies, but often finds he does not fully understand what they mean until time has passed.

"The good thing about being an artist, the best thing, maybe, is that you can take all of the hardest experiences in your life and put it into your work and it just makes you better," he said. "If you're willing to face it all, be honest about it all and show up vulnerably with those feelings and allow for the fact that you might not be able to really fully understand them, but you're willing to put them into what you're making, it's a blessing. For me, it's the only way that I can understand what's happening in my own life."

A release date for Company has not yet been announced.

articles.title: La ‘pullita’ de Broncano a Borja Iglesias tras ser campeón del Mundial: “Jugó tres minutos y ganó la misma copa que Rodri”
articles.standfirst: El futbolista del RC Celta fue protagonista en el segundo programa de ‘La Revuelta’, de la 1 de RTVE
articles.summary: El futbolista del RC Celta fue protagonista en el segundo programa de ‘La Revuelta’, de la 1 de RTVE
articles.body: ‘La Revuelta’ ha vuelto a La 1 de RTVE este martes, 8 de septiembre, con el segundo programa de su tercera temporada. El espacio de la cadena pública, comandado por David Broncano, recibió a Borja Iglesias a través de videollamada, jugador del RC Celta y actual campeón del Mundo con España, en el Teatro Albéniz, ubicado cerca de la Puerta del Sol tras dejar atrás el Teatro Príncipe Gran Vía. En primera instancia, el presentador quiso destacar su primera entrega de este lunes, 7 de septiembre: “Hicimos una buena audiencia, pero no mejor que ‘El Hormiguero”. Tras ello, presentó al futbolista: “Más o menos es un campeón del Mundo, es jugador, pero se ha lesionado, siempre le pasa de todo, no ha podido venir y nos ha atendido desde casa. Ha venido de jugar 3 minutos en el Mundial y es campeón del mundo, increíble”. Tras ello, apareció el futbolista desde su domicilio de Santiago de Compostela: “Quiero pedir perdón, que he tenido que volverme a Vigo a tratarme, no estoy lesionado”. Tras ello, el presentador le dijo lo siguiente: “Que te recuperes y te esperamos cuando puedas. Estás invitado”, a lo que contestó el jugador del cuadro vigués: “Espero que antes de marzo por si acaso…”, en referencia a si hay elecciones, cambio de Gobierno y el programa acaba cambiando de canal, algo de lo que ya habló Broncano estos días. Regresando al tema del Mundial, Iglesias reveló que fue “un verano intenso”, pero que “mereció la pena”: “He rentabilizado los tres minutos que jugué en el Mundial para sumar un título más en el palmarés”. “Ha ganado la misma copa que Rodri jugando tres minutos. Tiene los mismos mundiales que Messi”, comentó David Broncano entre risas al respecto. Posteriormente, pusieron un video de las mejores jugadas del delantero en el torneo, en las que se vio ir a presionar, no controlar un balón que le mandó Unai Simón y hacer de DJ en la fiesta del título, a lo que añadió él mismo: “Toqué un solo balón, buen vídeo habéis hecho, me encanta”. “Ha sido muy bonito, la gente se ha identificado con un grupo que ha sido muy variado. Se vio una victoria de grupo, de equipo”, añadió acerca del hito del grupo de Luis de la Fuente. Para finalizar, el presentador de ‘La Revuelta’ dijo que Borja está entre los 30 mejores jugadores del mundo por el hito y que está invitado en el futuro, a lo que sentenció Iglesias: “Fue un placer, espero asistir el día que cancelen la vistia de alguien”.

articles.title: Head of Smithsonian museums announces he will be stepping down
articles.summary: The US institution is under pressure from the Trump administration to change how it portrays the country’s history.
articles.body:
The head of the Smithsonian Institution will be stepping down from his position by the end of the year, following pressure from the administration of United States President Donald Trump.

In a statement on Tuesday, Lonnie Bunch announced he was leaving the institution, an organisation that oversees one of the world’s largest collections of museums and educational and research centres.

“I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward,” Bunch said.

“It is time for my next chapter, a chapter that will allow me to continue to protect the integrity of the Smithsonian and to champion the importance of a history that illuminates and celebrates the complex story of our nation.”

Many of the Smithsonian’s museums occupy a place of pride on the National Mall in Washington, DC.

But since the start of Trump’s second term as US president, the institution has come under increasing fire from conservatives who object to its depictions of racism, colonialism and other aspects of US history.

While the Smithsonian does not fall under the president’s direct authority, a large part of its budget comes from the federal government, and the Trump administration has threatened to sever that funding stream over the institution’s alleged “anti-American ideology”.

In July, Trump had ordered the US Department of the Interior to erect “warning signs” near the entrance to the National Museum of American History to inform visitors about the museum’s alleged bias.

In August, the Interior Department also sent a letter to the Smithsonian detailing its criticism if the institution did not address its concerns by changing its top leadership.

“Because these concerns arise from executive leadership and institutional ideology at the Smithsonian, the appropriate response must likewise address executive leadership and institutional ideology,” the letter said.

The Smithsonian museums are free for the public to visit, and they draw millions of people each year.

They include the National Air and Space Museum, National Museum of American History, National Museum of the American Indian, National Museum of Natural History and National Portrait Gallery.

Bunch was appointed as the secretary of the Smithsonian in 2019, becoming the first African American to serve at the helm of the 180-year-old institution.

He previously served as director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, which opened in 2016 after a years-long effort.

But the Trump administration has sought to crack down on institutions it accuses of promoting left-wing “woke” ideology and movements like diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI), a social justice initiative to encourage the participation of marginalised groups.

As part of that effort, Trump has sought to exert greater control over programming at cultural institutions like the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, one of the US capital’s most prominent theatre venues.

He has also ordered probes of other entities, from schools and universities to the military and national parks, in an effort to rid federally supported institutions of what he called “discriminatory” DEI practices.

The Smithsonian, however, was an early target of the Trump administration’s anti-DEI campaign.

Within months of taking office in 2025, Trump issued an executive order titled “Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History”, which called for changes to ensure the Smithsonian returned to its “rightful place as a symbol of inspiration and American greatness”.

The White House, at the time, accused the Smithsonian’s American Art Museum and National Museum of African American History and Culture of promoting narratives that portrayed US values as harmful and oppressive.

In May 2025, Trump also said he had fired Kim Sajet, the director of the National Portrait Gallery, a Smithsonian museum, after he accused her of being a “highly partisan person, and a strong supporter of DEI, which is totally inappropriate for her position”.

Critics, however, argued that Trump did not have the authority to fire Sajet, who resigned under pressure in June of that year.

Further controversies erupted when the Smithsonian removed references to Trump’s two first-term impeachments from exhibits, before reversing course amid public outcry.

Soon after, in August 2025, the White House wrote to Bunch’s office saying it would conduct a review of the museum’s content, including its exhibits and social media content, to ensure the narratives shared would “celebrate American exceptionalism”.

Bunch has remained under pressure since that time, facing the prospect of balancing the institution’s funding requirements with the need to shield itself from political interference.

In the wake of his resignation on Tuesday, historians and artists like director Ken Burns voiced their support for the outgoing Smithsonian head.

“Lonnie Bunch is a great historian, public servant and a dear friend,” Burns wrote on social media.

“He has devoted his career to helping us understand the full American story in all its complexity. Our country is better for his work, and I am deeply grateful for it.”

articles.title: Luis de la Fuente se moja y señala a los herederos de Messi y Cristiano Ronaldo: "Están en otra dimensión..."
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador español cuenta en 'El Hormiguero' cómo vivió el Mundial
articles.summary: El seleccionador español cuenta en 'El Hormiguero' cómo vivió el Mundial
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente ha visitado este martes 'El Hormiguero' para hablar de la selección española, del éxito conseguido en los últimos años y de su libro 'La vida se entrena cada día'. El seleccionador ha repasado algunos de los momentos más importantes de su etapa al frente del combinado nacional y también ha explicado cómo gestiona uno de los aspectos más delicados de cualquier vestuario: los egos y las posibles 'estrellitas' entre sus jugadores. Pablo Motos le ha preguntado directamente si en algún momento ha tenido que poner los pies en la tierra a alguno de sus futbolistas. De la Fuente ha reconocido que sí, aunque ha dejado claro que intenta hacerlo sin generar conflictos dentro del grupo. El técnico ha ido un paso más allá al explicar qué ocurre cuando un futbolista no acepta sus planteamientos o resulta imposible reconducir su comportamiento dentro del grupo. "Si alguno ha sido irreconducible, no ha vuelto", ha sentenciado De la Fuente. La frase deja entrever la firmeza con la que el seleccionador gestiona el vestuario, aunque durante la entrevista no ha señalado a ningún jugador concreto. De hecho, ha defendido en varias ocasiones el comportamiento del grupo que ha construido en la selección española y ha asegurado que sus futbolistas destacan no solo por su nivel deportivo. "Son los mejores deportistas y las mejores personas", ha aseverado. También ha explicado que una de sus estrategias para poder tomar decisiones sin dejarse influir por el ruido exterior consiste en no consumir información sobre sí mismo ni sobre la selección. El técnico ha reconocido que no lee los medios de comunicación porque considera que las críticas terminan afectando a cualquiera, incluso aunque intente mantenerse al margen. "Quien dice que no le afecta lo que digan de él, no lo creo. Siempre afecta algo", ha explicado. Por eso, De la Fuente ha optado por no leer lo que se publica sobre su trabajo. Según ha contado, esta decisión le permite tomar determinadas decisiones con mayor libertad, incluso aquellas que pueden generar debate fuera del vestuario, como dejar a determinados futbolistas en el banquillo. Con la retirada internacional de Lionel Messi y la cada vez más cercana de Cristiano Ronaldo, Pablo Motos también ha preguntado a De la Fuente por los futbolistas que considera llamados a recoger el testigo de las dos grandes estrellas de las últimas décadas. El seleccionador español no ha dudado al señalar a Kylian Mbappé y Lamine Yamal como los dos jugadores que, a su juicio, están un escalón por encima del resto. "Es bueno para el fútbol que haya varios jugadores con proyección para que mejoren esos deportistas", ha explicado De la Fuente antes de mencionar al delantero francés y al internacional español. "Mbappé, Lamine... Son futbolistas con una dimensión diferente", ha asegurado. El técnico también ha citado a otros nombres como Raphinha o Jude Bellingham, aunque ha establecido una diferencia entre ellos y los dos primeros: "Después hay grandes jugadores como Raphinha, Bellingham... Pero Mbappé y Lamine tienen otra dimensión".

articles.title: Nesta quarta, começa o XV Festival de Cultura e Gastronomia em Macaé | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento gratuito reúne 25 chefs, opções a partir de R$ 25, aulas de culinária e atrações culturais até domingo na orla da cidade.
articles.summary: Evento gratuito reúne 25 chefs, opções a partir de R$ 25, aulas de culinária e atrações culturais até domingo na orla da cidade.
articles.body:
Evento começa nesta quarta com pratos exclusivos e atrações na orla — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Está oficialmente aberta a temporada de sabores em Macaé. Começa nesta quarta-feira (9) o XV Festival Macaé de Cultura e Gastronomia, transformando a charmosa orla da Praia dos Cavaleiros no ponto de encontro mais gostoso da região. Durante cinco dias de festa, até domingo (13), moradores e visitantes têm um convite irrecusável para passear à beira-mar, apreciar boa música e saborear criações incríveis preparadas por 25 chefs e 23 estabelecimentos locais. Com entrada gratuita e estrutura ocupando cinco quadras, o evento é perfeito para curtir com a família e os amigos, lembrando que menores de 14 anos precisam estar acompanhados dos responsáveis.

A grande estrela desta edição é o conceito “Terroir”, que promete encantar o paladar do público celebrando a cozinha de território. As receitas valorizam a história local, utilizando ingredientes adquiridos na própria cidade para criar pratos repletos de identidade. O menu completo é uma verdadeira tentação e conta com 18 opções de entradas, 18 pratos principais, lanches e cinco sobremesas, com preços bem acessíveis a partir de R$ 25. Dá para escolher entre delícias como risoto com lagostinha grelhada, porco assado no rolete ao fogo de chão, paella de picanha, polvo na brasa, massas artesanais, comida oriental, pizzas, hambúrgueres e cheesecakes irresistíveis.

Cozinha Show, área para crianças e estandes de produtores locais completam a festa — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Além da comidinha de primeira, o festival chega recheado de novidades para garantir a diversão de todos. Quem passar por lá poderá conferir a área Boulevard, um espaço exclusivo dedicado a empreendedores e produtores da região, além de se refrescar com opções de duas vinícolas, três bares de drinks, quatro cervejarias artesanais e sete pontos de venda de chope.

Para os amantes da culinária que querem colocar a mão na massa, o espaço Cozinha Show traz aulas práticas e degustações gratuitas com feras da gastronomia nacional e internacional, como Frédéric Monnier, Bruno Katz e Vanessa Rocha. A programação ainda inclui um espaço infantil para os pequenos e atrações culturais para animar a noite.

A festa já está rolando e você não pode ficar de fora dessa celebração de cultura e sabor. Nesta quarta e quinta-feira, as atividades vão das 18h às 23h; na sexta-feira (11), a diversão começa às 18h e vai até a meia-noite. No fim de semana, a estrutura abre mais cedo para você aproveitar o dia inteiro: no sábado (12), das 13h à meia-noite, e no domingo (13), das 13h às 21h. Venha vivenciar essa experiência gastronômica e prestigiar o melhor da cultura e dos talentos de Macaé na Praia dos Cavaleiros.

articles.title: Agendamento de sessões de cinema inclusivo na Cultura | G1
articles.standfirst: O Projeto “Som do Silêncio Azul” é destinado às pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA).
articles.summary: O Projeto “Som do Silêncio Azul” é destinado às pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA).
articles.body:
Projeto Som do Silencio Azul — Foto: Divulgação

Para garantir o acesso à Cultura de forma plena e em um espaço preparado para acolher pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista, que podem apresentar hipersensibilidade auditiva, visual ou dificuldade de adaptação a ambientes convencionais, a Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura, em parceria com o Museu da Imagem e do Som, está fazendo o agendamento de pequenos grupos para assistir a sessão do cinema inclusivo, dentro do Projeto “O Som do Silêncio Azul” .

Os interessados em agendar as sessões de cinema inclusivo devem comparecer à sede administrativa da Fundação, localizada na Avenida Cristóvão Barcellos, 109 – Centro, de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 17h . Mais informações pelo telefone 2764-7115.

De acordo com a presidente da Fundação, Rosemarie Teixeira, a ideia é promover uma experiência sensorial adaptada a pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista e fornecer o acesso à arte cinematográfica em um ambiente acolhedor, com controle de

luminosidade, sonorização reduzida e liberdade de expressão durante as sessões. “Vamos fazer as sessões com agendamento para grupos escolares e grupos dos programas de Saúde. A ideia é garantir opções de entretenimento para todos”, declarou.

A parceria com o Museu da Imagem e do Som contribuirá para ampliar a qualidade da programação, democratizar o acesso a obras audiovisuais e fortalecer a formação de público para o cinema inclusivo, possibilitando uma programação qualificada e contribuindo para a construção de uma cidade mais acolhedora, diversa e culturalmente acessível para todos

SELEÇÃO DE FILMES – A seleção de filmes será por películas de curtas e longas-metragens de temática leve, preferencialmente sem excesso de estímulos visuais e sonoros. O cinema silencioso e obras com forte narrativa visual terão destaque, favorecendo a linguagem universal das imagens e expressões. Os filmes serão selecionados no acervo da Tela Brasil, plataforma do audiovisual brasileiro.

articles.title: Mestrinho retorna ao Rock in Rio e quer mostrar o 'forró em sua essência purinha' no festival | G1
articles.standfirst: Em 2024, sanfoneiro mesclou clássicos de forró com sucessos lendários do rock. Mas, desta vez, quer levar seu forró, incluindo faixas do projeto Dominguinho.
articles.summary: Em 2024, sanfoneiro mesclou clássicos de forró com sucessos lendários do rock. Mas, desta vez, quer levar seu forró, incluindo faixas do projeto Dominguinho.
articles.body:
Mestrinho canta no Forró Caju em Aracaju. — Foto: PMA

No Rock in Rio 2024, Mestrinho estreou no festival e mostrou toda sua habilidade com a sanfona na abertura de sua apresentação, mesclando acordes de clássicos de forró, como "A Volta da Asa Branca" e "Que Nem Jiló", com sucessos lendários do rock, como "Love of My Life" e "We Are The Champions", do Queen, e "Sweet Child O' Mine", do Guns N' Roses.

Neste ano, o artista de 37 anos, que foi o primeiro sanfoneiro a ter um show solo no Rock in Rio, repete sua participação no evento. Ele se apresenta no Palco Global Village, no dia 12 de setembro. Mas, desta vez, ele deixará o rock para os artistas do gênero. ( Veja programação completa do festival. )

“Ali [em 2024], como foi o meu primeiro Rock in Rio, eu estava chegando, e quis mostrar um pouco dessa versatilidade que muitas pessoas assistiram e viram. Agora eu vou chegar com o forró na sua essência purinha mesmo, que eu amo", contou Mestrinho em entrevista ao g1 .

Mas a abertura de seu show de estreia no evento não foi aleatória, já que Mestrinho também é fã de rock e de estrelas como Queen, Beatles e David Bowie.

"E ali eu quis mostrar o tanto que o instrumento, o acordeon, a sanfona, é universal. Ela pode tocar qualquer gênero, se você tiver a sensibilidade de entender o que cada gênero pede e a sutileza de introduzir os instrumentos sem agredir nenhum dos gêneros, só mostrando a beleza do acordeon.”

Mestrinho no Rock in Rio — Foto: Cristiano Juruna

O Rock in Rio conta com estrelas do forró desde sua primeira edição, em 1985, quando incluiu Elba Ramalho e Alceu Valença em sua programação.

Para Mestrinho, o espaço dado para o gênero no evento atualmente é "satisfatório".

"Eu acho que tudo tem a sua dosagem certa ali. E o festival sempre mostrou que tem, sim, como misturar. Ele se chama Rock in Rio, mas é um festival de música. E não perdeu sua essência, porque tem muita banda de rock, a galera está sempre ali", analisa o sanfoneiro.

"Se for para entrar mais [forró] , a gente vai agradecer, vai curtir demais, mas não é uma coisa que a gente bate o pé."

Para Mestrinho, sua presença no evento é consequência do amor que ele tem pelo gênero, pela música e por sua versatilidade em transitar por vários gêneros.

"Sou um artista que vem do forró, mas pretendo não ser um artista rotulado de uma coisa só", diz.

"Dominguinhos, que é uma das minhas maiores inspirações, transitou em tudo o que é gênero. E Gilberto Gil também, que é uma das minhas grandes [inspirações]. Você vê o Gilberto Gil fazer disco de reggae, de vários gêneros. E ele é o Gilberto Gil. Não é o Gilberto Gil de um gênero ou de outro. Eu me inspiro muito nisso."

Os dois artistas não são referências distantes para Mestrinho. O músico tocou com Dominguinhos e Gil desde o início da carreira. Seu trabalho mais recente com Gil foi a "Última Turnê" do artista. E ele trabalhou com Dominguinhos por muitos anos antes de sua morte, em 2013 .

"Tive o prazer de trabalhar com Dominguinhos, e também de ter uma grande amizade. É meu ídolo. Eu tocava o acordeon de um jeito antes de conhecer ele, e depois que eu o conheci, mudou totalmente a minha visão do instrumento."

Projeto Dominguinho chega a Salvador — Foto: @kaiocads

Dominguinhos, inclusive, é homenageado no "Dominguinho", que colocou Mestrinho em outro patamar da carreira. Lançado em abril de 2025, o projeto reúne o sanfoneiro com João Gomes e Jota.Pê. O trio já está com sua segunda turnê pelo Brasil.

"O 'Dominguinho' é um marco muito importante na minha carreira, na minha vida. Mudou muita coisa. Eu já tinha uma carreira estabilizada no sentido financeiro, já conseguia viver do meu próprio trabalho com folga, graças a Deus, por algo que eu já tinha conquistado. E esse algo que eu conquistei é que me levou ao Dominguinho", afirma Mestinho.

O sanfoneiro ainda cita que o projeto mudou sua vida em diversos aspectos, incluindo o emocional.

"O Dominguinhos só foi possível por conta da nossa amizade. Não foi uma coisa que o João, o Jota, olharam para mim e falaram: 'ele toca muito, ele é muito maravilhoso, então vou chamar ele para agregar nesse trabalho'. Não. Foi: 'cara, eu gosto tanto de você, a gente tem uma afinidade muito grande, vamos gravar 4 músicas aí para celebrar isso'."

"Então quando eu penso no Dominguinho, eu penso, claro, nas pessoas que estão mudando também suas vidas, num Brasil que está enxergando o forró de novo de uma forma grandiosa. Mas também penso no quanto é valioso o nome Dominguinho relacionado a amizade de nós três."

Até por isso, Mestrinho garante que seu show no Rock in Rio vai contar com faixas do projeto.

"Não tem como eu subir no palco hoje sem tocar algo do Dominguinho. A gente vai celebrar muito essa coisa do Dominguinho ter alcançado o que alcançou."

E depois de se apresentar, Mestrinho deve correr para acompanhar a apresentação de João Gomes junto com a Orquestra Brasileira no Palco Sunset.

Mestrinho, João Gomes e Jottapê — Foto: Globo

Por vezes, o Dominguinho é comparado ao Tribalistas, projeto lançado em 2002 e que reúne Arnaldo Antunes, Carlinhos Brown e Marisa Monte.

Para Mestrinho, a comparação é um elogio. "Foi um dos projetos mais marcantes no nosso país, com três pessoas super talentosas."

A diferença dos Tribalistas talvez seja sua longevidade. Arnaldo, Carlinhos e Marisa se reuniram para projetos pontuais. Primeiro, para a gravação do álbum, em 2002. Na época, fizeram raras apresentações em conjunto. Quinze anos depois, lançaram um segundo álbum e anunciaram a tão esperada turnê, em 2018. Em seguida, deixaram seus fãs órfãos novamente.

"A nossa intenção é envelhecer juntos e continuar, com certeza. Mas a gente tem que deixar os planos da vida tomarem conta, porque o João tem o seu trabalho, o Jota tem o dele, e eu tenho o meu."

"Eu não posso prometer que vai ter Dominguinho a vida inteira. A gente planeja o nosso futuro, mas no fim das contas, nós somos feitos de momentos. Resumindo, só o tempo vai dizer o quanto que a gente vai continuar, mas a nossa intenção é permanecer."

Então vem terceiro álbum por aí, Mestrinho? "Eu espero que sim."

Mestrinho — Foto: Felipe Giubilei/Divulgação

articles.title: Documentário sobre Elon Musk usa IA para simular entrevista com declarações polêmicas do bilionário | G1
articles.standfirst: Produção usa avatar digital e voz sincronizada por inteligência artificial para recriar uma entrevista com base em falas que o bilionário já deu em outras ocasiões.
articles.summary: Produção usa avatar digital e voz sincronizada por inteligência artificial para recriar uma entrevista com base em falas que o bilionário já deu em outras ocasiões.
articles.body:
Montagem com o cineasta Alex Gibney, à esquerda, e Elon Musk. — Foto: AP Photo

Um novo documentário sobre Elon Musk usa um avatar criado por computação gráfica e sincronização de voz com inteligência artificial para simular uma entrevista com o CEO da SpaceX e da Tesla , utilizando declarações que ele realmente fez em outras entrevistas.

A escolha foi intencionalmente irônica, segundo o cineasta Alex Gibney, que falou sobre o filme nesta terça-feira (8), em Veneza, antes da estreia mundial da produção. A estratégia faz referência à ideia defendida por Musk de que todos nós vivemos em uma simulação e, ao mesmo tempo, provoca suas opiniões consideradas paradoxais e mutáveis sobre a tecnologia .

Gibney afirmou que o objetivo é transmitir a “realidade do que ele fez e a irrealidade de sua narrativa”.

Os cineastas consultaram advogados antes de avançar com a ideia e receberam autorização para usar o avatar de Musk.

O cineasta vencedor do Oscar esteve no Festival de Cinema de Veneza acompanhado de Ashley St. Clair, uma ex-influenciadora conservadora que tem um filho com Musk e aparece no filme. Ela fala sobre o relacionamento entre os dois, a personalidade do empresário e o acordo de confidencialidade que lhe foi apresentado — e que ela se recusou a assinar — para garantir o pagamento de pensão relacionada à paternidade.

“Foi-me oferecida a oportunidade de não falar por US$ 40 milhões”, disse ela.

No início deste ano, St. Clair também processou a empresa de inteligência artificial de Musk, alegando que o chatbot Grok permitia que usuários criassem imagens falsas de teor sexual envolvendo ela . Segundo ela, as imagens provocaram humilhação e sofrimento emocional.

O filme também aborda a aquisição do X por Musk e o que Gibney descreve como uma manipulação do algoritmo da plataforma.

“Uma coisa que eu não entendia corretamente quando comecei o filme era como Musk ajustou os algoritmos do Twitter para, na verdade, priorizar a hostilidade e o ódio em vez daquilo que deveria ser uma praça pública”, afirmou Gibney.

A repórter da revista Wired Zoë Schiffer, que também participa do documentário, acrescentou que “ ele ajustou o algoritmo, tanto para reduzir a presença do jornalismo tradicional quanto para ampliar alguns dos comentários e vozes mais inflamatórios da plataforma ”.

St. Clair disse acreditar que Musk está alimentando conflitos e “provocando uma divisão deliberada que poderia ser catastrófica se não fosse regulamentada ou contida”.

Com quase quatro horas de duração, Musk aborda a infância traumática do empresário, incluindo uma entrevista com seu pai, Errol Musk. O documentário também acompanha os primeiros anos de Musk no Vale do Silício, seu trabalho no DOGE durante o segundo governo de Donald Trump e sua atuação na política de direita internacional .

Segundo Gibney, o filme seria muito mais curto antes de Musk se envolver na campanha de Trump.

Entre os entrevistados estão Martin Eberhard, cofundador da Tesla; Justine Musk, primeira mulher de Musk; o neurologista Sam Harris; a jornalista de tecnologia Kara Swisher; e Samantha Power, ex-administradora da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID).

O documentário também aborda preocupações sobre as informações coletadas sobre cidadãos americanos pelos integrantes do DOGE, que tiveram amplo acesso a diversas agências do governo dos Estados Unidos.

O filme “Musk” será lançado nos cinemas em outubro.

articles.title: 'Toxic' box office collections day 14: Yash, Kiara Advani, Tara Sutaria starrer film earns Rs 69 lakhs; second Tuesday sees 8% drop
articles.summary: Yash starrer 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' continued its run at the box office on its 14th day. The film recorded an India net collection of Rs .
articles.body: Yash starrer 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' continued its run at the box office on its 14th day. The film recorded an India net collection of Rs 69 lakhs on its second Tuesday. According to Sacnilk, the collection came from 1,290 shows across the country.The latest figure marks another decline for the action drama. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' had collected Rs 75 lakhs on its second Monday. The Day 14 earnings therefore represent an 8.0% drop from the previous day's collection.'Toxic' India box office crosses Rs 247 crWith its second Tuesday earnings added, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has reached an India net collection of Rs 247.19 cr. The film's India gross collection currently stands at Rs 295.02 cr.The film has been witnessing a sharp slowdown after its first week. It recorded Rs 239.30 cr during its opening week. Its daily earnings have dropped considerably during the second week, with the film now struggling to remain above the Rs 1 cr mark.'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' opened strongly at the box office, collecting Rs 101.10 cr on Day 1. However, the Yash starrer witnessed a sharp decline from its opening-day figure over the following days.The film earned Rs 37.65 cr on Day 2, followed by Rs 27.20 cr on Day 3. Its weekend collections stood at Rs 25.15 cr on Saturday and Rs 23.00 cr on Sunday. The movie then saw a major drop on its first Monday, collecting Rs 7.65 cr. It recorded a slight improvement on Tuesday with Rs 7.85 cr.By the end of its first week, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' had accumulated Rs 239.30 cr.The second week brought a much steeper decline. The film collected Rs 5.45 cr on its second Wednesday and Rs 4.25 cr on Thursday. Its second Friday collection fell to Rs 1.75 cr, before Saturday and Sunday saw modest improvements at Rs 2.28 cr and Rs 2.42 cr, respectively.The film then dropped below the Rs 1 cr mark on its second Monday. It earned Rs 75 lakhs that day, followed by Rs 69 lakhs on its second Tuesday.Overall, the box office trajectory shows a massive opening followed by a consistent slowdown. After reaching Rs 239.30 cr in its first week, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' added only Rs 12.84 cr from Days 10 to 14. Its second-week weekday performance has been considerably weaker than its opening phase.Worldwide gross reaches Rs 338.32 crThe Geetu Mohandas directorial has also earned from markets outside India. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has collected Rs 43.30 cr from overseas markets so far. When the India and overseas gross figures are combined, the film's worldwide gross collection reaches Rs 338.32 cr.Kannada and Hindi versions report different occupancyThe Kannada version remained the larger contributor to the film's Day 14 India net collection. It earned Rs 47 lakhs, while the Hindi version added Rs 22 lakhs.'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' recorded an overall occupancy of 18.7% on Tuesday. The Kannada version registered 16.52% occupancy. Its morning shows recorded 11.64%, followed by 21.73% in the afternoon. Evening and night shows registered 14.64% and 14.18%, respectively. articles.summary: La televisiva ha acudido al espacio de RTVE para responder a las preguntas de Broncano
articles.body: Este martes, 8 de septiembre, ‘La Revuelta’ ha tenido invitados por partida doble. En primer lugar, el campeón del mundo Borja Iglesias, que fue el protagonista de una videollamada con Broncano. Tras la entrevista al jugador del Celta de Vigo, llegó el turno de Carmen Lomana. Tras su visita como público en la primera temporada, ahora era ella quien se sentaba en el sofá. Lejos de rehuir las cuestiones de David Broncano, Lomana respondió todo aquello que el presentador quería saber, incluidas sus relaciones en el último mes. Es cierto que la televisiva se hizo de rogar. “Es que no me atrevo”, empezaba dudando. No obstante, la insistencia del público fue empujando poco a poco a la colaboradora de algunos espacios de RTVE. “Tampoco estoy todo el día. Es que ya ni me acuerdo…”, seguía dubitativa Lomana. Por un momento, parecía que iba a ser capaz de evitar la cuestión incluso: “¿Tan precarios sois? Que tenéis que llevar las veces que lo hacéis apuntadas”. De todos modos, la televisiva se lanzaba y daba la respuesta que todos estaban esperando: “Ha sido un buen mes. Tres a la semana es cosa sana”.
